transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-05
Time: 15:00 - 15:48 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood CSM), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Maya Torres (AnchorWave Head of Product), Aidan Cho (Platform Eng Lead), Sofia Patel (Security), Noah Reed (Program Manager)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
AnchorWave wants to use Redwood Dedicated for customer-facing routing and a private VPC for PII pipelines. They have strict KMS and audit requirements, need SSO, and want to start with a 4-week pilot limited to the returns-processing microservice. Performance targets: p95 < 220ms for simple prompts, burst to 200 qps during peak.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you carving out time. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Maya Torres: Hey Jordan, Maya here.
[00:08] Aidan Cho: Aidan on the call.
[00:10] Sofia Patel: Sofia, security.
[00:12] Noah Reed: Noah here.
[00:13] Priya Raman: Priya from Redwood CSM.
[00:15] Ethan Park: Ethan, Redwood SE.
[00:18] Jordan Lee: Great. Objective today is launch readiness kickoff, make sure we align on success criteria, what we need from you, and a rough timeline. I'll hand over to Maya to ground us in what AnchorWave is trying to solve.
[00:30] Maya Torres: Cool. So we handle logistics returns for retailers, our customers want faster authorization and triage. We built a microservice that calls LLM for classification and response generation, and currently it's prototype on another provider. We're pushing toward a pilot in front of real users but need better latency and cost predictability. Also, the legal team wants data residency and audit logs.
[00:52] Jordan Lee: Understood. On the Redwood side we usually recommend Dedicated for production-facing workloads where you need predictable throughput and data isolation. We also have Private (VPC/on-prem) if you need the control plane in your VPC.
[01:06] Aidan Cho: Quick question — how different is Dedicated vs Private from an integration standpoint? Network wise and auth?
[01:12] Ethan Park: Good question. Dedicated is managed infra owned by Redwood but can be isolated to your tenant, we offer VPC peering or private endpoints depending on region. Private is the package we deploy into your VPC or on-premises — that gives you full network control and local KMS. For most customers who want low ops and still need isolation we do Dedicated + VPC endpoints.
[01:38] Sofia Patel: For us, KMS capabilities matter a lot. Can Redwood support HSM-backed keys or at least bring-your-own-key? Also retention policies and audit logs — we need log retention for 2 years.
[01:50] Priya Raman: Yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations across major cloud providers. HSM-backed can be arranged in Private mode; in Dedicated we can integrate with your cloud KMS but HSM-specific vendor would be part of a deeper architecture review. Audit logs are available and we can export to your logging stack. Two-year retention is possible as an add-on.
[02:18] Noah Reed: Budget and timeline — we want pilot to start late August and go live early November. Budget is mid-range but we need numbers to lock.
[02:28] Jordan Lee: Makes sense. For timeline I'd suggest a 4-week pilot scope: week 1 integration and auth, week 2 validation and data mapping + initial low-traffic tests, week 3 performance/load tuning, week 4 pilot review and rollback/cutover plan. That would put pilot start around 2026-08-24 if you want late Aug.
[02:50] Maya Torres: That aligns. Success criteria: functional parity with prototype, p95 latency under 220ms on standard prompts, accuracy stability within +/-3% of current model, and cost within 20% of our target.
[03:06] Ethan Park: Noted. We'll capture those as the pilot SLAs in the runbook.
[03:12] Aidan Cho: On the performance side, our current prototype uses batching but it's inconsistent. Does Redwood have recommendation for batching config versus latency SLO?
[03:22] Ethan Park: Yes, Redwood Optimize recommendations are tailored per workload; you can trade off batching size for latency. For low-latency microservices we often recommend dynamic batching with small max batch sizes and KV-caching for common prefixes. We'll share suggested config and a benchmark harness.
[03:40] Aidan Cho: Perfect. On telemetry — we need token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route. Can we get that in console?
[03:48] Priya Raman: Absolutely, Console has per-route dashboards and token breakdowns, and we can add retention for traces. We'll turn on the route-level telemetry for the pilot.
[03:58] Sofia Patel: About compliance, do you have SOC2 reports or ISO certs we can share with legal? And how do you handle data deletion requests?
[04:10] Jordan Lee: We can share SOC2 Type II and ISO attestation. For deletion, we have configurable retention and deletion APIs; in Private you control the logs and data. We'll send the compliance packet after this call.
[04:24] Maya Torres: Great. A couple of technical constraints — our infra is primarily GCP with a private VPC, and we use HashiCorp Vault for secrets. We also have an internal SSO via SAML.
[04:38] Ethan Park: All standard. For GCP we can do VPC-SC or private endpoints; we integrate with Vault for secret bootstrapping when in Private mode, and SAML SSO is supported for console access. We'll need a short network diagram from Aidan to propose VPC connectivity options.
[04:58] Aidan Cho: I'll pull a diagram. Also curious on fallback behavior — if Redwood Dedicated capacity is saturated, can we automatically fallback to a cheaper model or another region?
[05:08] Jordan Lee: Yes, smart routing policies can fallback to model variants or different tiers to maintain availability — we can configure canary failover to a slightly higher latency but cheaper model, or route to a different region that meets residency constraints if allowed. We will include fallback policies in the runbook.
[05:28] Noah Reed: For load testing, what should our ramp look like? We have projected peak bursts of 200 qps for a 5-minute window, and steady state 40 qps.
[05:38] Ethan Park: We'll provide load test scripts. Recommended ramp: start at 5 qps, step up to 40 qps across 15 minutes, then run burst windows to 200 qps for 5 minutes, validate p95 and error rates. We'll want to run that in a staging environment with production-like model sizes.
[05:58] Maya Torres: One last legal ask: can logs be redacted before leaving our VPC? We need to prevent PII from being stored outside retention windows.
[06:08] Priya Raman: We can configure client-side redaction or tokenization; in Private deployments it's easier since you control the pipeline. For Dedicated we have pre-ingest hooks and masking tools. We'll include options in the security runbook.
[06:28] Jordan Lee: Good. Let's talk roles and ownership so we don't have dangling items. Priya will own runbook delivery and onboarding schedule. Ethan will own the load test artifacts and architecture review. I'll own pricing and contract items.
[06:40] Priya Raman: I'll follow up with a runbook template and a calendar invite for weekly syncs.
[06:46] Aidan Cho: Who should I send the network diagram to?
[06:49] Ethan Park: Send it to me and cc Priya.
[06:52] Sofia Patel: I'll compile SOC2 questions and KMS needs and send an itemized doc.
[06:56] Jordan Lee: Perfect. Any other questions?
[07:00] Maya Torres: Not right now. Can we get a cost estimate for Dedicated for initial pilot capacity? Rough ballpark is fine.
[07:06] Jordan Lee: We'll send T-shirt sizing and a detailed estimate after we confirm the expected token volumes and model family. For now, expect mid-range reserved pool pricing with an optional burst buffer.
[07:18] Noah Reed: One more — do you provide a sandbox account for our devs to iterate without touching production quotas?
[07:24] Priya Raman: Yes, we can set up a sandbox project with lower quotas and separate billing tags. We'll include instructions in the runbook.
[07:32] Jordan Lee: OK let's recap next steps and owners.
[07:36] Jordan Lee: Action items — send runbook, pricing, compliance packet; customer to send network diagram, SOC2 questions, and pilot prompts/test cases. Schedule architecture deep-dive.
[07:48] Maya Torres: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[07:50] Jordan Lee: Thanks all, we’ll follow up with docs.
[07:53] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: speaker overlap and some labels may be off; certain product names auto-transcribed (e.g., "Redwood Dedicated" -> "Redwood Dedi") and proper nouns occasionally garbled.

End of transcript.
